name: deepagents-evolution
description: Nine checkpoints from deepagents' real 1.11 to 1.12 core cycle (July 2026). Exercises discovery (delete protocol, filesystem allowlist, middleware-merge-by-name), changed-knowledge correction (filesystem path errors, write_file semantics, default base prompt, opt-in todo middleware), and a full remove-then-revive of the structured system prompt so complete forgetting and later re-discovery of identical knowledge are both scored.

checkpoints.label: recoverable errors for invalid/denied filesystem paths (#693)

versions.statement: The library's primary entry point is the exported createDeepAgent function, which constructs and returns a ready-to-run LangGraph agent.
The agent's built-in filesystem tools are read_file, write_file, edit_file, ls, glob, and grep.
The agent exposes a task tool that delegates work to sub-agents, each running with its own isolated context.
The deepagents package publishes environment-specific entry points: the default "." export plus dedicated "deepagents/node" and "deepagents/browser" exports.
LangChain runtime packages such as @langchain/core and @langchain/langgraph are declared as peerDependencies, so a consumer installs them alongside deepagents rather than receiving them bundled.
Storage is abstracted behind a Backend protocol with swappable implementations, including StateBackend, FilesystemBackend, StoreBackend, and CompositeBackend.

The createDeepAgent systemPrompt option accepts a structured configuration object (SystemPromptConfig) with optional prefix, base, and suffix parts that are assembled in that order, in addition to accepting a plain string or SystemMessage.

The createDeepAgent systemPrompt option accepts a structured configuration object (SystemPromptConfig) with optional prefix, base, and suffix parts that are assembled in that order, in addition to accepting a plain string or SystemMessage.
The backend protocol includes an optional file deletion operation that returns a structured DeleteResult, letting a backend report the outcome of a delete rather than only succeeding or throwing.
The filesystem middleware accepts a tools allowlist that restricts which built-in filesystem tools are exposed to the model.
Custom middleware passed to createDeepAgent replaces a built-in default middleware that shares the same name, rather than being appended alongside the default.
When a filesystem tool is given an invalid or disallowed path, the tool throws an error.
When a filesystem tool is given an invalid or disallowed path, the tool returns a recoverable error result to the model instead of throwing, so the agent can react and continue.
write_file only creates a new file; when the target path already exists the tool refuses the write and returns an error directing the caller to edit the existing file or write to a new path.
write_file creates the file when it does not exist and completely overwrites it when it does; the caller does not need to read an existing file before replacing it.
The agent applies an authored default base system prompt, and its built-in middleware and tool descriptions carry prescriptive usage guidance by default.

There is no authored default base system prompt; the base prompt is empty by default and the built-in tool descriptions are concise, retaining only load-bearing guidance while custom prompts, skills, and memory remain intact.
By default the agent includes todo-list planning middleware, so the write_todos planning tool is available without any opt-in.
The todo-list planning middleware is opt-in and is not part of the default middleware stack, so write_todos is only available when a caller explicitly enables it.
